The Threat Landscape
WHY TRADITIONAL
SECURITY
FAILS AGAINST AI
AI systems introduce novel attack vectors that traditional security tools and methodologies cannot detect or prevent. Understanding these threats is the first step to defending against them.
Prompt Injection
Attackers manipulate LLM inputs to bypass safety guardrails and extract sensitive data or execute unauthorized actions.
Model Extraction
Adversaries steal proprietary AI models through careful querying, replicating months of training investment.
Data Poisoning
Training data manipulation introduces backdoors that activate under specific conditions, compromising model integrity.
Jailbreaking
Sophisticated prompts override safety mechanisms, enabling AI systems to produce harmful or policy-violating outputs.

What is Certified Offensive AI Security Professional (COASP)?
The Certified Offensive AI Security Professional (COASP) is an advanced AI security certification designed to train professionals in offensive AI security and real-world AI system testing. It focuses on identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities across AI models, applications, and infrastructure using a structured AI system hacking methodology. This AI security course prepares learners to simulate real-world attacks on modern AI systems and secure them effectively.
What is Offensive AI Security and how does the COASP course cover it?
Offensive AI security is the practice of testing AI systems by simulating real-world attacks to uncover vulnerabilities before they are exploited. The COASP AI red team certification approaches this through a structured methodology aligned with real attack scenarios, covering prompt-based attacks, adversarial machine learning, model extraction, and attacks on data and training pipelines. It also extends into developing areas like agentic AI, ensuring that professionals understand how to both exploit and secure AI systems in practice.
How is the COASP course different from other AI security certifications?
Many AI security courses focus on theory or general awareness, but COASP is designed as a hands-on offensive AI security certification. It focuses on AI attack surfaces, AI system hacking methodology, and real-world testing across models, pipelines, and agentic systems, backed by 30 lab exercises, 20+ offensive AI techniques, and alignment with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP LLM Top 10.
What AI threats are covered in the COASP certification?
The AI security program covers a wide spectrum of AI-specific threats across the entire AI lifecycle, including prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, adversarial inputs, model extraction, data poisoning, backdoor attacks, and supply chain vulnerabilities, along with emerging risks in agentic AI systems. An offensive security professional completing this course will also work through 15+ MITRE ATLAS techniques, covering real-world attack patterns such as LLM jailbreaking, crafting adversarial data, and ML inference exfiltration.
Which AI security and governance frameworks are covered in the COASP curriculum?
The COASP curriculum is aligned with globally recognized AI security and governance frameworks such as MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ensuring alignment with industry standards and real-world security practices.
Which AI security tools and techniques are covered in the COASP course?
This COASP course introduces 20+ tools used across reconnaissance, vulnerability assessment, and adversarial testing, including but not limited to PyRIT, Garak, Burp Suite, and the Adversarial Robustness Toolbox. Explore the full tools and techniques list here.
What makes COASP the most offensive, hands-on AI security certification?
COASP is a highly practical, hands-on AI security certification built for offensive security professionals. It follows a structured three-phase offensive methodology that covers reconnaissance, exploitation, and defense, applied across real AI systems. It includes 20+ offensive AI techniques, 20+ AI security testing tools, and 30 lab exercises, making it one of the most comprehensive, practice-driven AI security certifications available today.
What are the COASP AI security certification exam details?
The COASP AI security certification exam is a 6-hour, live-proctored assessment consisting of 70 questions, including 65 multiple-choice questions and 5 practical, performance-based challenges. It tests hands-on skills across offensive AI attack techniques including prompt injection, agent hijacking, model extraction, data poisoning, and supply chain attacks.
Which key skills are validated with AI security certification?
The COASP AI security certification validates skills including AI attack surface mapping, prompt injection testing, adversarial machine learning, model extraction, data poisoning detection, agentic AI exploitation, and AI incident response, aligned with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP LLM Top 10 frameworks.
What career roles does the COASP certification prepare me for?
The COASP AI security certification prepares offensive security professionals for 20+ career roles including AI red team specialist, adversarial AI engineer, offensive security engineer, AI threat hunter, AI security architect, AI incident response engineer, adversarial ML researcher, AI security analyst, AI test and evaluation specialist, and MLOps/AIOps security specialist, among others.
Why are AI Security Certifications worth it in 2026?
AI security certifications are worth considering in 2026 because organizations are rapidly adopting AI while facing new risks such as prompt injection, data poisoning, model abuse, and governance challenges. These certifications help professionals validate in-demand skills, stay current with evolving threats, and strengthen career opportunities in a fast-growing security market. For many learners, the value depends on career goals, hands-on learning quality, and industry recognition.
What AI-focused OSINT techniques are covered in AI security certifications such as COASP?
AI security certifications such as COASP and Certified LLM Security Professional programs cover advanced OSINT techniques focused on AI reconnaissance and attack surface mapping. Offensive security professionals can explore how to identify and profile AI assets, gather intelligence from training data pipelines, map publicly exposed AI attack surfaces, enumerate AI endpoints, services, and APIs, and analyze models or vector stores from an attacker’s perspective. COASP also covers exposure mitigation, hardening controls, AI threat intelligence, and continuous monitoring to improve defensive readiness.
What access period comes with the COASP certification package?
COASP learners receive 6 months of access to official labs to practice AI red teaming techniques, offensive testing workflows, and hands-on security scenarios. Training resources including the official e-book and video modules on iLearn are accessible for 1 year, supporting flexible self-paced learning. The exam voucher is also valid for 1 year from the evaluation submission date, giving candidates sufficient time to prepare and schedule their certification exam.
Does COASP certification expire and how many ECE credits are required to maintain it?
COASP certification remains valid through EC-Council’s continuing education (ECE) framework and renewal requirements. Professionals are required to earn 120 ECE credits over a 3-year ECE cycle to maintain their certification status.
Is COASP an industry-recognized AI security certification?
Yes, COASP is an official EC-Council certification, globally recognized for its focus on offensive AI security, AI red teaming, LLM exploitation testing, and securing agentic AI systems.
Is 24/7 support available for COASP learners?
Yes, COASP candidates have access to 24/7 learner support for assistance with training access, learning resources, and platform-related queries.
